sections.h2: Who collects property tax in Madison County, NY?
sections.html:
In Madison County, most town and county bills are collected by the local town tax collector, while the county Treasurer takes over unpaid balances and collects directly for four towns. The Treasurer's office is in the County Office Building at 138 N. Court Street in Wampsville, and the county's Real Property Tax Services office handles assessment questions and tax maps.

Madison County sits just east of Syracuse, and Wampsville is the county seat. The county has 15 towns, the City of Oneida, and villages that include Canastota, Cazenovia, Chittenango, Hamilton, Morrisville and Wampsville. Each of those pieces can show up on a single bill, so the first job when you plan to sell is to learn which collector holds your parcel.

  • Fenner, Georgetown, Hamilton and Lincoln: the county Treasurer collects town and county tax from January 1 until the bill is paid or the parcel is foreclosed.
  • Other towns: the town tax collector accepts payment through April 30.
  • City of Oneida: the city collects throughout the whole cycle. Its Chamberlain's Office answers questions at 315-363-7399.
  • Delinquency questions outside a payment period: call the Treasurer at 315-366-2371.

sections.h2: When are Madison County tax bills issued and what does interest cost?
sections.html:
Town, city and county bills go out on January 1, village bills on June 1 and school bills on September 1. A missed bill does not excuse the tax: the county says interest and penalties cannot be waived because a bill never arrived, so call the collector if nothing shows up in the first week.

Interest on unpaid town and county tax starts February 1 at 1% per month. After April 30 the unpaid balance returns to the Treasurer, who adds a 5% county return penalty on the original tax while the 1% monthly interest keeps running. A town may also add a notice fee. The Treasurer mails updated amounts due from time to time, so a payoff figure you were quoted in spring can be out of date by closing.

School tax follows its own path. The county explains that the school tax collector sends the Treasurer a list of unpaid school taxes on or before November 15, which means a school balance can join the county's delinquent file a few weeks from today.

sections.h2: How long before Madison County forecloses on unpaid tax?
sections.html:
Madison County moves a delinquent parcel through roughly three tax years before an auction, with notices and added fees at each stage. The county posts the steps on its Taxes page, and the table below condenses them.

Madison County delinquent tax timeline, from the county Taxes page
StageWhat the county does
February 1, year oneInterest of 1% per month begins on unpaid town and county tax
After April 30Balance goes to the Treasurer with a 5% return penalty
Early NovemberList of unpaid taxes recorded with the County Clerk
July 1, year two$250 fee per delinquent parcel and a lien search
January to July, year twoCertified and first-class notices to owners and lienholders, then newspaper advertisement before July 31
April, year threePosting of parcels lacking proof of service, adding $100
July to August, year threeInspection, damage letters, then Order of Foreclosure sent to Madison County Supreme Court
September, year threeAnnual auction, usually the third Saturday

Source: Madison County Taxes page. Once the advertisement has gone to the newspapers, the county does not pull a parcel from it because of a later payment, so pay before that step if you can.

sections.h2: What can I do if my Madison County assessment looks too high?
sections.html:
Start with your town assessor, because Madison County's assessment office points owners there first. The county's guidance says to ask the assessor how your value was set and what comparable sales were used, and to bring an independent appraisal by a New York certified appraiser if you have one.

If the assessor does not move, you can take evidence to the town's independent Board of Assessment Review on Grievance Day. The state's rule for most communities is the fourth Tuesday in May, which falls on May 25 in 2027, though you should confirm with the assessor. A homeowner who still disagrees can then use Small Claims Assessment Review. New York's tax department puts the filing fee at $30 and sets a window of 30 days from the filing of the final roll.

  • Exemption applications go to your assessor by March 1 (May 1 in the City of Oneida).
  • Tax map questions go to the county's Real Property Tax Services, which generally changes maps only when a certified survey exists.
  • The county office cannot give legal advice or run a survey, so use an attorney for deed or boundary questions.

sections.h2: What does Madison County look like for a seller?
sections.html:
Madison County is mostly rural, with suburban pockets along NY Route 5 near Syracuse and in Cazenovia. The Census Bureau estimates the population at 67,120 in July 2025, spread over about 655 square miles of land, and counts 31,048 housing units.

Owners live in 78.3% of homes, the median owner-occupied home was valued at $184,600 for 2020 to 2024, and median household income was $75,499. Monthly owner costs with a mortgage ran $1,615. Those figures matter for a seller because a modest home value makes a few thousand dollars of penalties and fees a larger share of the price than it would in a pricier county.

School district boundaries cut across town lines here, with districts such as Oneida, Canastota, Chittenango, Hamilton and Cazenovia among those listed for the county. Match your parcel to its school district when you read a bill, since the school levy is billed on its own September 1 cycle.

sections.h2: How do I sell a Madison County house that owes back taxes?
sections.html:
Ask the Treasurer for a written payoff before you accept any offer, because penalties, the $250 lien-search fee and the $100 posting fee change the total. Then pick a closing date that falls ahead of the next county step, such as the July advertisement or the September auction year.

A buyer who pays cash and takes the house as-is can often close on a short timeline, which helps when a tax deadline is close. If the parcel has already been advertised, the county will not remove it for a late payment, so compare the sale date with the advertisement date first. Redemption is another route: New York's RPTL 1110 allows a delinquent lien to be redeemed by paying the lien and charges within the redemption period, which is two years after the lien date unless the notice sets a later date.

  1. Call 315-366-2371 and request the current balance by parcel.
  2. Check whether your property is in one of the four county-collected towns or in Oneida.
  3. Choose a sale route that closes before the next notice or fee date.

faqs.q: Who do I call about delinquent taxes in Madison County?
faqs.a: Call the Madison County Treasurer's Office at 315-366-2371. For the City of Oneida, the City Chamberlain's Office at 315-363-7399 handles it. The county lists both numbers on its Real Property Tax Services FAQ.

faqs.q: What penalty applies after April 30 in Madison County?
faqs.a: A 5% county return penalty is added to the original tax once the balance goes back to the Treasurer, and interest continues at 1% per month. A town notice fee may also apply if the town charges one.

faqs.q: When is the Madison County property auction?
faqs.a: The county generally holds its auction in September of the third year of delinquency, usually on the third Saturday. The Board of Supervisors then typically votes on the sales in October. Ask the Treasurer for the current year's date.

faqs.q: Does missing the tax bill stop interest?
faqs.a: No. The county states that interest and penalties are not waived because a taxpayer did not receive a bill. Contact the local tax collector if a bill has not arrived within a week of issue.

faqs.q: Can I still file an exemption this year?
faqs.a: Exemption forms are due to your assessor by March 1, or May 1 in the City of Oneida, and that date has passed for 2026. The next deadline is March 1, 2027, and the forms are on the state tax department website.
